**Last Updated: August 4, 2026**

> The WSL2 dev-environment showcase that briefly replaced this file lives at [docs/wsl2-environment.md](docs/wsl2-environment.md).

A living list of what's done and what's left on this fork. This is a self-hosted-only fork of Coolify — the goal is a clean, no-frills, enterprise-friendly self-hosted deployment platform with no billing/marketing surface area.

## At a glance

This file is long and detailed on purpose — every claim below is backed by evidence (line numbers, exact commands, verification steps), not just asserted. That detail is useful if you want to check a specific claim, but it's not built for skimming, so here's the skim version first.

**Done, in full:**

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Livewire→React migration | 84/84 pages, complete 2026-07-14 — see "Livewire → React/Inertia migration" below |
| PHPStan baseline hardening | 1,306 → 55, 65 phases — see "PHPStan baseline reductions" below |
| De-commercialization | Billing/Stripe fully removed |
| Security hardening | CodeQL + Psalm, 11 real CVEs patched, 2 real findings fixed — see "GitHub repo-level security features" below |
| Laravel backend audit | Team-scoping, Sanctum tokens, cross-device reachability — see "Laravel backend improvements" below |
| Manual QA smoke-test checklist | All 11 sub-issues closed 2026-07-29, every SSH-touching action browser-confirmed — see "Manual QA smoke-test checklist" below |
| ESLint `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` cleanup | All 20 findings resolved individually (per-effect review, not a bulk fix), baseline at 0 as of 2026-07-31 — issue #33 closed. See "Frontend component testing" below |

**Actually still open, right now:** 17 items — see the overview table at the top of **Still to do** below.

If you only read one section of this file, read this one and that table — everything else is the evidence trail behind them.

### PHPStan baseline milestones

Every phase touched the baseline, but only these actually found something — a real, previously-invisible bug, or a structural fix big enough to collapse dozens of duplicate entries at once. Everything else was routine typing; this table is the "what actually mattered" subset of the full phase table above.

| Phase | Commit | Milestone |
|---|---|---|
| 6 | `1e38eae09` | Largest single-phase baseline drop of the whole initiative (1609 → 1323, −286): typing 6 widely-shared traits (`HasStandaloneDatabaseCommon`, `HasSafeStringAttribute` ×18 consumers, etc.) collapsed dozens of duplicate per-consumer entries into one. |
| 9 | `7d80d50d0` | Largest drop by absolute count (1244 → 1062, −182). Real bug fixed: a missing guard before calling `githubApi()` on an unsupported source-provider type now fails gracefully instead of type-erroring. |
| 11 | `510eb46e8` | Real bug fixed: `envStore()`/`envUpdate()` now return a graceful error/404 when a resource has no `environment_variables()` relation, instead of a fatal method-call-on-generic-`Model` error PHPStan's typing had been masking. |
| 13 | `07e19e27a` | Real fatal bug: `customizeName()` and the `mountPath()`/`hostPath()` setters read `Stringable`'s **protected** `$value` property directly from an unrelated class — every call would have thrown a fatal `Error`. Fixed with the public `->toString()`. |
| 22 | — | Real bug fixed, TDD'd: `EmailChannel::send()` crashed with `strtolower(): ... null given` on a nullable `smtp_encryption` column — every sibling `smtp_*` field already null-coalesced, this one didn't. |
| 25 | `7c5263640` | 2 real bugs, both TDD'd: `isConfigurationChanged()` hashed full model instances instead of `pluck('value')`, making the "sorted for determinism" config hash actually order-dependent; and `ServiceExtraFieldsResolver`'s `$SERVICE_*` closures never captured `$service` and read a protected `Stringable::$value` — would fatal the instant a field value started with `$SERVICE_`. |
| 26 | `47bd8b8f6` | Real bug fixed, TDD'd: neither `ServiceApplication` nor `ServiceDatabase` cast `is_log_drain_enabled` to boolean — a fresh-from-DB instance returned SQLite's raw `int(1)`/`int(0)`, and declaring the accessor `: bool` would have thrown under `strict_types=1`. |
| 30 | `eb3c1cafa` | Real bug fixed: `Team::sources()`'s `Collection<GithubApp>::merge(Collection<GitlabApp>)` used the wrong `Collection` class (Eloquent's model-invariant one instead of `Illuminate\Support\Collection`) — found twice, independently, once in `sources()` and once in a `deleting` event closure. |
| 33 | `b6443e257` | 2 real bugs: a permanently-dead SSL-cert-param branch on 3 database engines that never actually had an `ssl_mode` column; and `databaseType()` was `public` instead of `protected`, so Larastan couldn't recognize it as a valid computed Attribute property despite working fine at runtime. |
| 41 | `91f88653b` | 2 real bugs, TDD'd: `loadComposeFile()`'s stale-domain pruning always took its truthy branch (a `Collection` is always truthy in PHP) so `docker_compose_domains` could get permanently stuck at `"[]"` instead of reverting to `null`; and 4 call sites string-compared `getMorphClass()` instead of using `instanceof`, blocking type narrowing. |
| 42 | `6a084c314` | Real fatal-shaped bug, TDD'd: `Server::status()` called the `services()` relation **method** directly in a `foreach` instead of `->get()`-ing it first — a relation builder isn't `Traversable`, so the loop body silently never executed, and a downed server's Service-based resources never got marked `'exited'`. |
| 45 | `2298b4243` | Real bug fixed, TDD'd: `forceDeployService()` tried to mark stuck activities as errored via `$activity->properties->status = ...` — `properties` is a `Collection`-cast attribute, so this set a dynamic property on the Collection object itself and never persisted. Fixed by reassigning the attribute via `->put()`. |
| 50 | `3cfe828de` | Structural fix, largest drop since Phase 6 (361 → 225, −136): converted `App\Contracts\StandaloneDatabaseInstance` from a plain interface to an abstract class, since Larastan never resolves PHPDoc through an interface. Migrated all 8 database engines and 27 consuming files; caught a real runtime `TypeError` in a test fixture still typed against the deleted interface (63 failing tests surfaced it immediately). |
| 52 | `d082d1ae0` | Real dead code removed: `SslCertificate`'s `application()`/`service()`/`database()` relation methods were unused everywhere — every real caller reads the raw `resource_type`/`resource_id` columns directly — so they were deleted rather than typed. |
| 56 | `103d4e01c` | The most severe bug found this session, TDD'd: `ServerLimitCheckJob::handle()` read `$this->team->limits`, a property that has never existed on `Team` (the real column is `custom_server_limit`) — Eloquent's magic getter silently returned `null`, and PHP's `-` operator treated it as `0`, so **every team with at least one server would have had all of them force-disabled** on every run. The job is never actually dispatched anywhere in the current codebase (confirmed via grep), so it never fired in production — but the fix has lasting value if it's ever wired up. |
| 60 | `1d9233c7a` | 2 real bugs: `CleanupStuckedResources.php` called the `destination()` relation **method** instead of the property on 4 of 7 engine blocks, so an orphaned-destination cleanup branch could never fire for those engines (masked by an adjacent, differently-worded check catching the same case); and `StandaloneRedisFactory` still wrote a `redis_password` column a migration had dropped over a year earlier — `StandaloneRedis::factory()->create()` had been silently broken the whole time, never exercised by any existing test. |
| 64 | `d8c4ccb25` | Real, TDD'd production bug: `ApplicationPreview::generate_preview_fqdn_compose()` passed a nullable `docker_compose_domains` column straight into `json_decode()` with no null guard — under this codebase's `strict_types=1`, the very first preview-fqdn generation for any fresh docker-compose application would crash before generating a single domain, across all 6 real call sites. |

**What's left in the 55-entry baseline (2026-07-19 audit, updated after Phase 65):** all 55 are confirmed PHPStan/Larastan false positives, individually verified, not assumed — nothing neglected.

| Category | Entries | Why it's a false positive |
|---|---|---|
| Trait per-class-context artifact | 26 (`instanceof.alwaysFalse` ×12, `catch.neverThrown` ×11, `booleanOr.alwaysFalse` ×3) | `ClearsGlobalSearchCache.php` is shared by 13 models — PHPStan analyzes the trait once per consuming class with `$this` narrowed to that concrete type, so a check relevant to a *different* consumer gets flagged "always false" even though the trait needs that branch for its other real consumers. |
| `Illuminate\Support\Collection`'s non-covariant `TValue` template | 11 (`return.type` ×10, `argument.type` ×1) | `dumpType()` (Phase 62) confirmed the declared and actual shapes print as structurally identical, yet PHPStan still rejects it — a documented upstream limitation, not fixable without loosening real types. Mostly `SettingsScheduledJobsController.php` + `TerminalController::getAllActiveContainers()`. |

Root cause, two parts: (1) three user-creation paths never set `email_verified_at` — the first/root user (`CreateNewUser`), team-invited users (`TeamController::sendInvitation`), and OAuth signups (`OauthController::callback`); (2) in non-cloud mode, `DecideWhatToDoWithUser`'s own unverified-email redirect only runs when `isCloud()`, so unverified users fell straight through to Laravel's stock `verified` middleware, which hardcodes a redirect to `route('verification.notice')` — a name this app never registered (it used `verify.email` instead, predating that Laravel convention). Affected the very first (root) user on any genuinely fresh self-hosted install, any team-invited member's first login, and any OAuth signup's first login — the seeders happened to mask this by setting `email_verified_at` directly. Fixed by renaming the route to `verification.notice` (a *second* route registered as an "alias" for the same URI doesn't work — Laravel's `RouteCollection` keys `allRoutes` by method+URI, so it silently evicts the first from the name lookup) and auto-verifying new users in non-cloud mode (OAuth users always, since the provider already confirmed the email). 6 new tests (`EmailVerificationOnUserCreationTest.php`), TDD-proved via `git stash`/revert (4 of 6 failed with the exact real symptoms, restored clean). Worth knowing regardless: `applications` uses `nullableMorphs('destination')`, and Eloquent's `morphTo()` crashes on a null type instead of resolving to `null` (its "empty morph" placeholder builds a self-referential query with an empty owner key — Postgres rejects the empty identifier outright). | 2026-07-22 | Dev-environment infra, not app code, but tracked here since it's a real fix, not just documentation: the Docker Desktop/WSL2 post-reboot race (`DEVELOPING_IN_CONTAINERS_WINDOWS.md`'s documented `coolify` empty-mount issue) turned out to not be fully solved by the existing `autoheal` sidecar. Tested against two real reboots — including one *after* enabling Docker Desktop's "start on sign-in" setting, which fixes a different problem (Docker not running yet) but not this one. Both times, the race hit multiple containers at once, including `coolify-autoheal` itself (exited `127`) plus `mailpit`/`minio`/`vite`/`testing-host` — none of which had any `restart:` policy set at all, a real silent gap independent of this specific bug. Fixed, two parts: (1) `restart: unless-stopped` added to the 4 unprotected services; (2) `scripts/dev-up.sh`, a host-side detect-and-fix script — run once after logging back in following a reboot. A container-native auto-fix (`mount-doctor`, `restart: always`, no bind mount of its own besides the Docker socket) was built first, on the theory that a socket-only container would be immune to the race; a Windows Task Scheduler entry was considered and deliberately rejected in favor of it, for portability. A third real reboot disproved the theory: `mount-doctor` itself came up `Exited (127)`, alongside `coolify-autoheal`/`coolify-realtime`/`coolify-testing-host`. `docker inspect` on all four showed the real mechanism is broader than "directory mount attaches empty": *file* bind mounts (`docker.sock`, soketi's individual `.js` file mounts) fail OCI container-creation outright on reboot ("mounting a directory onto a file"), rather than merely attaching empty like directory mounts do — and `mount-doctor` needs `docker.sock` to do anything, so it's a victim of the exact failure it exists to repair. Nothing running inside a container can recover from a failure that happens before that container can be created; `mount-doctor` was removed, and `dev-up.sh` (host-side, immune to this class of race) is the real fix. A follow-up attempt to synthetically test the failure path (hiding `artisan` via `docker exec`) was itself a mistake — bind mounts have no separate container-side copy, so it moved the real host file; caught immediately, fully restored, confirmed byte-identical via `git status`. See issue #45. |

Not an app bug — `OauthSettingSeeder` (called from `DatabaseSeeder`) ran cleanly when invoked directly and created all 10 expected providers, so this was dev-data drift (this instance's data had simply never had the seeder run against it), fixed by re-seeding. | 2026-07-22 | Found via the `/settings/scheduled-jobs` smoke test (issue #21): the Skipped Jobs tab showed `docker cleanup` skipped every single scheduler run for the dev server, reason "Server not functional." Traced to `coolify-testing-host` — the container was `running` (a Docker Desktop upgrade+restart earlier this session brought it back up cleanly), but its `docker.sock` mount was a stale/broken socket internally: `docker version` showed a real Client block but a null Server block. This silently broke `ServerConnectionCheckJob`'s Docker-availability check, cascading into `Server::isFunctional()` returning false and every docker-cleanup run being skipped. A plain `docker restart coolify-testing-host` fixed it immediately; re-dispatching `ServerConnectionCheckJob` synced `is_usable` back to `true`. `scripts/dev-up.sh` updated to add a functional check specifically for this container — verifying `docker version`'s Server block is non-null, not just that container status is `running`, since "running" alone wasn't sufficient evidence the mount had actually reconnected. See `DEVELOPING_IN_CONTAINERS_WINDOWS.md`'s reboot-race section. |

### Laravel backend improvements

Not related to the Livewire→React migration — a separate, dedicated backend-quality pass, prompted by the user asking for a general Laravel-improvement audit of the repo (audited 2026-07-15). Findings are evidence-based (line/method counts, live `pg_indexes` queries, actual config values); a few initial suspicions (mass-assignment protection, `APP_DEBUG` defaulting unsafe in production, missing API rate limiting) were investigated and ruled out as non-issues. One further finding from this audit is deliberately left open, not a bug — see "Laravel backend improvements — still open" in **Still to do**.

**Entry format, 2026-08-01 onward**: each `Finding & fix` cell starts with a bold one-sentence headline stating the actual outcome, so skimming the column means reading the headline per row instead of the full paragraph. Entries before this date are unchanged — this wasn't applied retroactively (169 existing rows, disproportionate for a readability nicety).

| Item | Date | Finding & fix |
|---|---|---|
| PHPStan baseline: 1,306 → 55 suppressed errors | — | 65 phases/commits, all 55 remaining entries confirmed as analysis-tool limitations — see "PHPStan baseline reductions" above, not duplicated here. |
| `Application`/`Service` team-scoping: 3-hop relation join, not indexed | 2026-07-19 | `whereRelation('environment.project.team', ...)` on every team-scoped query, unlike `Server`/`Project`'s direct indexed `team_id`. Added an indexed `team_id` column to both tables + backfill + a `saving()` sync hook; converted 18 more `Service::whereRelation(...)` call sites too. `ServiceApplication`/`ServiceDatabase`/the 8 standalone-database models have the same pattern one level deeper — deliberately out of scope (separate future ticket). One known, deliberately-unfixed edge case: the sync hook doesn't fire if a `Project`'s `team_id` changes after creation (confirmed no real code path does this today). |
| Sanctum API tokens never expire | 2026-07-19 | Tokens already expire via an explicit per-token `$expiresAt` — the real gap was the "Expires in" dropdown defaulting to `''` (= "Never"). Changed the default to 90 days. Verified live via a headless-browser session. |
| App reachable from a machine other than the one running Docker | 2026-07-19 | 3 of 4 suspected blockers (Docker port binding, Sanctum stateful domains, CORS) ruled out with direct evidence. Real blocker: Vite's dev server hardcodes `localhost` into asset URLs via `VITE_HOST` — documented fix (`VITE_HOST=<LAN-IP>`), dev-only; production build unaffected. |
| `main` branch had no protection rules | 2026-08-02 | Prompted by a "check for holes" audit that also confirmed secret scanning/Dependabot/CodeQL are all still `enabled` live (the 2026-07-22 drift noted below hasn't recurred). `gh api repos/.../branches/main/protection` returned a plain 404 "Branch not protected" — every CI job existed and ran, but nothing actually required them to pass before a merge, and nothing blocked a force-push or branch deletion. Applied via `gh api` PUT: all 9 real CI checks (CodeQL, Analyze (javascript), PHPStan, Psalm, Pint, Prettier, Pest, Vitest, HTML5 validity) required and must be up to date with `main` before merging; force-pushes and branch deletion blocked. Deliberately left `enforce_admins: false` and did not add a required-review rule — this is a solo-maintainer repo where the same account both opens and merges every PR, so a required review would either block all future merges outright or be satisfied by a meaningless self-approval; discussed the tradeoff directly rather than silently picking one. The practical effect: today's actual workflow (CI-green solo merges, direct doc-sync commits) is unchanged, but any hypothetical outside contributor, or an accidental broken/force-push, is now genuinely blocked rather than merely discouraged. |

Merged (squash), confirmed the merge auto-triggered fresh Quality/CodeQL CI runs on `main` (both green), then rebuilt and restarted the `soketi`/`coolify-realtime` dev container and confirmed the fix is actually live in the running process (`/terminal/node_modules/ws` → `8.21.0`, container healthy) — merging the PR alone wouldn't have updated the already-built image. **Post-upgrade sanity check**: ran the existing `terminal-utils.test.js` suite (9/9 passing, unaffected by the `ws` bump) and, more importantly, drove a real Playwright session through `/terminal` against the live upgraded container — selected the seeded dev server, connected, got a genuine shell prompt (`root@...:~#`), typed a command character-by-character (many small WebSocket frames, a similar shape to the fragmentation pattern the vulnerability concerned, just not attack-scale) and confirmed the output streamed back correctly with zero console errors. | 2026-07-23 | Application Deployment smoke test (issue #21's "Hard bucket," in progress): triggering a real deployment against the seeded dev server immediately found and fixed **two real, severe bugs stacked back to back** — both explain why the SSH-touching deployment happy path has never been exercised successfully before now. (1) `ExecuteRemoteCommand::executeCommandWithProcess()`'s output callback wrapped `$output` through `str()->trim()` (an `Illuminate\Support\Stringable`), then passed it straight into `sanitize_utf8_text(?string $text)` — a `TypeError` under `strict_types=1` for any log line that doesn't happen to start with the box-drawing `╔` character (the one branch where string concatenation happened to cast it back). This crashed every real deployment on its first ordinary log line. Fixed with an explicit `(string)` cast at the call site; 2 new tests (`tests/Unit/Traits/ExecuteRemoteCommandTest.php`), TDD-proved against the pre-fix code (both failed with the identical real error). (2) With that fixed, the deployment got further and hit a second crash: `convertDockerRunToCompose()` passed its nullable `$custom_docker_run_options` straight into `preg_match_all()`'s `$subject` argument, another `strict_types=1` `TypeError` — but this time for the overwhelming majority of applications, since most never set custom Docker run options at all. `generate_compose_file()` (which calls this) is invoked from 11 different places across the deployment job (nixpacks, dockerfile, dockercompose, PR previews...), so this wasn't dockerfile-specific — it's core, universal deployment logic. Fixed with a `?? ''` null-coalesce before the `preg_match_all()` call; 2 new tests (`tests/Unit/Helpers/DockerHelpersTest.php`), also TDD-proved. | 2026-07-23 | Application Deployment smoke test, continued and closed out: with both prior crashes fixed, a real deployment against the seeded dev server now **actually succeeds end-to-end** (real `docker build`, real rolling update, real container started) — confirmed via Playwright watching the real deployment log stream. Confirmed both live-update checklist items directly, watching the DOM change with zero manual refreshes of any kind: the Deployment Show page's own 2s poll took a fresh deployment from "In Progress" to "Finished" entirely on its own; the Deployment Index page's 5s poll did the same for its deployment list. Deploy, Redeploy, Restart, Stop, and Force Deploy (without cache) were each individually triggered live and confirmed to actually do the real thing (real container stop/start, real status transitions) — not just render the right button. **While testing Stop, found and fixed a much bigger, systemic bug**: `composer.json`'s `autoload-dev.files` unconditionally loaded 3 test-fake files (`tests/Support/Fakes/{action_remote_process_overrides,database_action_overrides,model_remote_process_overrides}.php`) into *every* PHP process in this dev environment, not just test runs — since dev dependencies (and therefore `autoload-dev`) are always active locally (`APP_ENV=local`, distinct from `phpunit.xml`'s `APP_ENV=testing`). These files intentionally declare same-named functions inside real app namespaces (`App\Actions\Application`, `App\Actions\Database`, `App\Models`) so PHP's namespace-resolution rules make unqualified calls resolve to the fake instead of the real global implementation — a legitimate test-double trick, but only if scoped to actual test execution, which it wasn't. Confirmed impact: clicking Stop crashed with "Typed static property `Tests\Support\Fakes\RemoteProcessFake::$containers` must not be accessed before initialization," reachable from `StopApplication`, `StopApplicationOneServer`, and `CleanupPreviewDeployment` — real, user-facing, silently broken in every real dev request the whole time these fakes existed. Worse: the `App\Actions\Database` override shadows 9 real functions this way, including `isDev()` and `convertDockerRunToCompose()` — meaning this same session's earlier `convertDockerRunToCompose()` null-guard fix (see the entry above) was being silently bypassed for any code in that namespace, since real calls never reached the fixed implementation at all. Applied the proper fix, not a band-aid: removed all 3 files from `composer.json`'s `autoload-dev.files` (matching what 2 of the 3 files' own doc comments already said should happen — the loading-mechanism documentation itself was stale/wrong), ran `composer dump-autoload`, then added explicit `require_once` to the 16 real test files that had been silently relying on the eager load — centralized into the 2 shared test traits (`InteractsWithDatabaseActions`, `InteractsWithStartDatabaseProxy`) where 8 of those files already shared one, rather than duplicating the `require_once` across each individually. Full Pest suite (1245/1245), Pint, PHPStan, and `composer validate` all clean after. One operational gotcha worth knowing: a *running* Horizon worker doesn't pick up an autoloader fix just from `composer dump-autoload` or even `horizon:terminate` — PHP function definitions are permanent for a process's lifetime, and Horizon's worker processes are forked from (not freshly exec'd from) an already-running master, so the master process itself has to be killed and let `s6-supervise` restart it fresh before real requests stop hitting the stale, pre-fix function table. See issue #21. |

Root cause: `submitInvite()` called `useForm().post(url, { data: {...via:'link'}, ... })`, but `useForm().post(url, options)` doesn't support a `data` override in `options` — only `router.post(url, data, options)`'s middle positional argument does — silently dropping `via` from every real request. Worse in the preview scope: `EnvironmentVariable::booted()`'s own `created()` hook auto-mirrors every new non-preview var into a preview copy too, so the default seed alone produced *both* a non-preview and a preview row before either cloning loop even ran, and the existing preview-clone loop had the identical blind-insert problem stacked on top. Fixed both loops to delete any colliding row (same resourceable + key + scope) before inserting, deliberately not via `updateOrCreate`/`toArray()` — `value` is an encrypt-on-write/decrypt-on-read mutated attribute, and calling `toArray()` forces the decrypt mutator to run on the already-encrypted replicated data, crashing with `DecryptException: The payload is invalid.` (hit this directly while first attempting the fix); `replicate()` is what safely copies the raw encrypted value without touching either mutator, which is why the original code used it in the first place. New Pest test in `ProjectApplicationConfigurationTabsTest.php`, TDD-proved via `git stash`. Duplicate-name rejection, both clone destinations, tag/env-var carry-over, and the volume-data checkbox all confirmed correct afterward. **Found and cleaned up on teardown, not a bug**: `Project`/`Environment` deletion doesn't cascade to their applications/databases (2 orphaned rows found and removed) — same class of gap as the destination-cleanup finding earlier in this smoke-test pass. | 2026-07-25 | Dependabot found a real high-severity PostCSS vulnerability (`GHSA-r28c-9q8g-f849`, [alert #2](https://github.com/Terrence721/coolify-full/security/dependabot/2)) and auto-opened PR #53 (8.5.16 → 8.5.18): PostCSS auto-loads a "previous source map" from a `/*# sourceMappingURL=... */` comment inside parsed CSS, and the path join doesn't sandbox `../` traversal — a crafted comment can read an arbitrary `.map` file off disk, or an absolute path verbatim if `opts.from` isn't set. Checked reachability before merging rather than trusting the advisory blindly, same discipline as the `ws` DoS fix (issue #50): `postcss` is a direct dependency, but its only invocation anywhere in this repo is `postcss.config.cjs` via `@tailwindcss/postcss` for Vite's build-time CSS pipeline — a full grep of `app/`/`resources/` found zero direct `require`/`import` of it. It only ever parses this repo's own developer-authored CSS at build time; unlike `ws`, there's no runtime path where attacker-supplied CSS reaches it, so this one isn't currently exploitable in this app's actual usage. Merged anyway (squash, all 7 CI checks green first) since it's a free, patch-only bump with zero functional risk. Verified the fix is actually live, not just merged on GitHub: `docker exec coolify-vite yarn install --frozen-lockfile` picked up 8.5.18, confirmed in `node_modules/postcss/package.json`, and a real `yarn build` completed cleanly against the new version. | 2026-07-25 | Found by noticing a real discrepancy in the Security tab, not by trusting its own summary: 3 closed Dependabot alerts, but only 2 had a PR reference — `brace-expansion` (`GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg`/`CVE-2026-14257`, high, [alert #3](https://github.com/Terrence721/coolify-full/security/dependabot/3)) didn't. Its `created_at` and `auto_dismissed_at` are the exact same timestamp — a system dismissal, not a human one, most likely because the vulnerable version is several levels deep in the tree with nothing in our own `package.json` for Dependabot to bump directly, so it gave up rather than leaving an unfixable-by-PR alert open. The vulnerable version was still genuinely resolved in the committed `yarn.lock` (`brace-expansion@^5.0.5` → `5.0.7`, exactly the top of the vulnerable range) — confirmed directly rather than trusting the alert's closed status. The bug itself: `expand()` bounds result *count* (`max`, default 100,000) but not result *length* — chaining brace groups stays under `max` while every result grows with the group count, exhausting memory with an uncatchable fatal V8 OOM that `try/catch` can't stop. Reachability: comes in via `eslint`'s own `minimatch` dependency (`yarn why` confirms), pure dev-tooling, not reachable at runtime — same category as the PostCSS finding, fixed anyway since it's free and correct. Dependabot couldn't open a PR for this one itself, so fixed manually with a scoped Yarn `resolutions` override in `package.json` targeting the exact nested path, not a blanket override — there's a second, unrelated `brace-expansion@1.1.16` elsewhere in the tree (a different major version line via `eslint-plugin-react`'s own older `minimatch`) that a blanket override would have forced onto 5.0.8 too, for zero benefit since it's already outside the vulnerable range. Took 3 attempts to get the resolution syntax right, each verified against the real `yarn.lock`/`yarn why` output rather than trusted from `yarn install`'s exit status alone: an npm-overrides-style key errored outright (invalid Yarn Classic syntax), a single-level nested path silently resolved to the wrong location (left `5.0.7` still actually hoisted, just added a dead unused `5.0.8` entry), and the working form needed the full nested path from the direct dependency down through every intermediate package. Confirmed via `yarn why brace-expansion` that the real, in-use copy is `5.0.8`, not just that an entry exists somewhere in the lockfile. Full suites clean: `yarn lint` (the actual consumer) unaffected at the same 22-error baseline, Vitest 450/450, `yarn build` succeeds, `format:check` clean. See issue #55 (closed). |

| 2026-07-30 | **Fixed issue #84** (closed) the same day, on direct request. Made Vite's dev server itself serve over HTTPS whenever the self-signed cert exists (`vite.config.js`), instead of the per-request dynamic-origin approach floated as the "real fix" in the finding above — turned out unnecessary: an HTTPS page can load HTTPS assets from *any* origin without a mixed-content block, so Vite just needed to serve its existing single asset origin over HTTPS too, not match the page's own origin exactly. Kept fully conditional on the cert file existing, so the default plain-HTTP workflow (no cert generated) is unaffected. Also extended `generate-cert.sh` to read `VITE_HOST` from `.env` and add it as a SAN automatically (as an IP or DNS name), since the cert now needs to cover Vite's asset origin too, not just the main page's hostname — otherwise the browser shows a second, CN-mismatch-flavored warning on top of the expected "untrusted self-signed CA" one. **Verified via `curl`, not assumed**: asset tags now say `https://192.168.1.155:5173/...`; `https://192.168.1.155:5173/resources/js/app.js` returns real JS over a working TLS handshake; `openssl s_client` confirmed the cert's SAN lists `coolify-full.localhost`, `localhost`, and the LAN IP; plain `http://localhost:8000` (the default workflow) still loads cleanly with no regression. **One real trade-off, disclosed on the issue rather than hidden**: once the cert exists, Vite serves *all* its assets over HTTPS for every access path — a single dev-server process can't split HTTP/HTTPS per consumer — so opting into the friendly HTTPS URL also puts a one-time browser cert-warning click-through onto the plain `localhost:8000` workflow, not just the new URL. `yarn build` clean. |

| 2026-07-31 | Code review (issue #70): sixteenth finding, `app/Console/Commands/CleanupDatabase.php`. The `activity_log`/`application_deployment_queues` cleanup blocks chained `->orderBy('created_at', 'desc')->skip(10)` before both `->count()` and `->delete()`, inherited from the original upstream import, apparently intending to always keep the 10 most-recent-of-the-old rows as a buffer even when everything is past the retention window. Found while scanning `app/Console/Commands/` for other scheduled/destructive commands after the `AdminDeleteUser.php` finding above — an Explore subagent flagged it as a candidate, verified personally before acting on it. Both halves of the pattern turned out to be independently broken: (1) `->skip(N)->count()` compiles to a single-row aggregate query with `OFFSET N` — since a plain aggregate always returns exactly one result row, any `OFFSET >= 1` discards that row entirely, so `count()` returns 0 unconditionally regardless of real data, confirmed directly against a real table with 19 rows (`skip(0)->count()` → 19, `skip(1)` through `skip(20)` → 0, every time); (2) `->skip(N)->delete()` ignores the offset in the opposite direction — Postgres's query grammar (`PostgresGrammar::compileDelete()`) only special-cases `isset($query->limit)`, never `$query->offset`, so it's silently dropped from the compiled `DELETE`, deleting every matching row instead of preserving the buffer. `app/Console/Kernel.php:91` schedules `cleanup:database --yes` to run **daily** — every day this logged "Delete 0 entries" for both tables while actually deleting everything past the retention window, with no minimum-history buffer ever enforced; on a low-activity instance an entire table's history could be silently wiped to zero rows on a routine run that reports doing nothing. Initially posted the commit-comment finding with a since-corrected inaccuracy (first draft claimed the dry-run count "correctly honors the offset" — re-verification via direct SQL inspection showed it doesn't, it's unconditionally 0; edited the public comment to the accurate version before proceeding to the fix). Fixed by resolving the ids to keep explicitly (`->orderBy(...)->take(10)->pluck('id')`) and filtering via `->whereNotIn('id', $keepIds)` instead of `->skip(10)` — a plain `WHERE`, so both `count()` and `delete()` behave correctly and consistently. New `tests/Unit/Console/CleanupDatabaseTest.php` (3 tests, previously zero coverage for this command) — seeds 3 recent + 15 old `activity_log` rows and confirms the echoed count is the real number (5) rather than always 0, and that exactly the 10 most-recent-of-the-old rows survive; confirms nothing is deleted when `--yes` is omitted even though the count is still reported; confirms the same fix applied to `application_deployment_queues`. TDD-proved: reverting the fix breaks all 3 tests — SQLite's test driver throws a hard SQL syntax error on `OFFSET` inside a `count()` aggregate, an even more overt failure mode than Postgres's silent-zero behavior in production, but conclusive either way. Landed via real branch + PR #91 (merged). Full suites clean: 1268 Pest (was 1265), full `pint --test`/`phpstan analyse` (not `--dirty`) both clean. No JS touched. |

| 2026-07-31 | Code review (issue #70): fifteenth finding, `app/Console/Commands/AdminDeleteUser.php`. `Cache::lock($lockKey, 600)` acquires a 10-minute lock to prevent two operators running `admin:delete-user` for the same user concurrently, inherited from the original upstream import, then never refreshes it. Found while reviewing the sibling action classes the `DeleteUserTeams.php` fix (fourteenth finding, above) belongs to — `DeleteUserServers.php` and `DeleteUserResources.php` both already query teams fresh (`$this->user->teams()->get()`) and were reviewed clean, but `AdminDeleteUser.php` itself, the only real caller of all three, held a separate concurrency problem of its own. Between phases the command blocks on interactive `confirm()`/`ask()` prompts of unbounded human duration — up to 8 of them across Phases 1–5, all while the lock is held and a `DB::beginTransaction()` is open. A careful operator reading multi-page deletion previews before confirming something irreversible can easily exceed 10 cumulative minutes, at which point the lock silently expires mid-flight and a second operator (or the same one, in a second terminal, having lost track of the first run) can acquire it and start a fully concurrent deletion for the same user — exactly what the lock exists to prevent. Fixed by calling `$this->lock->refresh(600)` after each of the 5 phases completes, right before the next interactive wait begins. The property is typed against `Illuminate\Contracts\Cache\Lock` (the interface `Cache::lock()`'s return type declares), which doesn't expose `refresh()` — only the concrete `Illuminate\Cache\Lock` abstract class does (real Redis/Memcached/DynamoDb locks all extend it) — so the new `refreshLock()` helper narrows via `instanceof \Illuminate\Cache\Lock` rather than widening the property's declared type, and PHPStan accepts it without a baseline entry. This app's cache driver is Redis (`config/cache.php`'s default), whose `RedisLock::refresh()` is a real atomic Lua-script operation; the array/database drivers' `CacheLock` doesn't support refreshing at all and throws, caught the same way `releaseLock()` already handles its own errors. New `tests/Feature/Console/Commands/AdminDeleteUserTest.php` (4 tests, previously zero coverage for this command) — `refreshLock()` calls `refresh(600)` on a refresh-capable lock, is a safe no-op with no lock held, swallows exceptions from a non-refreshing driver, and a full `--auto-confirm` run against a plain user (no resources/servers, only their own auto-created personal team) completes end to end and releases the lock cleanly afterward. | 2026-08-02 | **[Code Review]** **Deleting a server with "delete all resources" checked orphaned the real remote containers instead of stopping them — the DB rows vanished cleanly while Docker kept running them, unmanaged, indefinitely.** Thirtieth finding, issue #70, `app/Actions/Application/StopApplication.php` + `StopDatabase.php` + `StopService.php` + `app/Models/Server.php` — **high, reliability — Tier 2: Core-Lifecycle Reliability**. The controller soft-deletes the `Server` row synchronously, then a queued `DeleteResourceJob` (usually a separate queue-worker process) calls these 3 actions later; `$destination->server` — a plain `belongsTo` — resolves `null` once the row is soft-deleted, and `$server->isFunctional()` on `null` threw an uncaught `Error` (not caught by `catch (\Exception $e)`), propagating to `DeleteResourceJob`'s outer `\Throwable` catch, which logs and rethrows — but its `finally` block force-deletes the resource regardless, so containers were never actually stopped. Fixed by falling back to a trashed-inclusive lookup (`$destination->server()->withTrashed()->first()`) instead of crashing. **A second, distinct bug surfaced while tracing this**: `StandaloneDocker`/`SwarmDocker`'s `getServerAttribute()` accessor routes through `Server::findCached()`, a static identity-map cache invalidated on the `updated` event — but `SoftDeletes` writes `deleted_at` via a direct query update that never fires `updated`, so a process that had already cached a server kept serving the stale pre-delete object after a delete (the opposite failure mode: silently wrong data instead of a crash). Fixed by also flushing the cache on the `deleted` event. Found via an Explore-agent sweep run under the priority order — Tier 1 came back clean, so this Tier 2 finding was the top pick. New/extended tests: `StopApplicationTest.php`/`StopDatabaseTest.php`/`StopServiceTest.php` each got a regression test that deletes a real, persisted server (never touched via the identity-map accessor beforehand, so it reproduces the realistic cross-process scenario) and confirms the action still reaches and stops the real container; new `tests/Unit/Models/ServerIdentityMapTest.php` (3 tests, previously zero coverage for this cache) covers the identity-map fix directly. TDD-proved: reverting all 4 source fixes together reproduces the exact real symptoms across all 4 test files (uncaught `Error`; stale non-null cached object), then restored. Landed via real branch + PR #108 (merged, [`f23619f0c`](https://github.com/Terrence721/coolify-full/commit/f23619f0c)). Full suites clean: 347 Stop/Server/Delete-scoped Pest tests pass, full `pint --test`/`phpstan analyse --memory-limit=1G` clean. No JS touched. |

| 2026-08-02 | **[Code Review]** **Any admin/owner of the root team could download any other team's real database backup by guessing a small sequential integer ID — a live cross-tenant data exfiltration, not a hypothetical.** Thirty-first finding, issue #70, `routes/web.php` (`download.backup` route closure) — **critical, security — Tier 1: IDOR / cross-tenant data exfiltration**. The route only enforced `$team->id === $execution_team_id` when the caller's currently-selected team wasn't team 0 — the root team, an ordinary real team on any self-hosted multi-team instance, not exclusive to a formally-privileged "instance admin" role. `User::isAdminFromSession()` returns true for anyone admin/owner of team 0 regardless of which team is currently selected, so switching current team to 0 (a normal UI action) and hitting the route bypassed team-ownership checks entirely; `executionId` is a bare sequential integer with no relation to the caller (a real `uuid` column exists on the model but isn't used here). Checked whether "team 0 = instance admin" is established elsewhere — it is, but always scoped to instance-level settings, never another team's actual resources; every other resource-access path (including the sibling backup-upload route) scopes strictly by team with no exception. Found via an Explore-agent sweep run under the priority order — the first Tier 1 finding since several consecutive Tier 2 fixes, confirming the tiered sweep still finds real critical bugs rather than having exhausted them. Fixed by removing the team-0 exemption entirely; ownership is now enforced unconditionally. New `tests/v4/Feature/DownloadBackupTest.php` (3 tests, previously zero coverage for this route) — the root-team exploit path, the same IDOR for an ordinary non-root admin, and a same-team request confirming the fix doesn't reject legitimate access. TDD-proved: reverting the fix reproduces the exact real exploit (the root-team request skips authorization and reaches the SFTP layer, failing there with a 500 instead of 403, proving the boundary was bypassed), then restored. Landed via real branch + PR #109 (merged, [`693a48db0`](https://github.com/Terrence721/coolify-full/commit/693a48db0)). | 2026-08-03 | **[Code Review]** **The most severe finding this session — any admin-configured OAuth provider could be used to log in as an arbitrary existing user just by asserting their email, no password needed.** Forty-fourth finding, issue #70, `app/Http/Controllers/OauthController.php`, `bootstrap/helpers/socialite.php` — **critical, security — Tier 1: broken authentication / account takeover**. `callback()` resolved the target user via `User::whereEmail($email)->first()` and called `Auth::login($user)` with no check that this specific OAuth identity had ever been associated with that account — the `users` table has no `provider`/`provider_id` column at all, so login-by-email was the entire trust boundary. Reachable via `GET /auth/{provider}/callback` (`auth.callback`), fully public and unauthenticated — registered outside every middleware group in `routes/web.php`. Concrete exploit: an instance admin enables a self-hosted or admin-configured OAuth provider (GitLab, Authentik, Zitadel, etc.); an attacker registers on that external IdP using a victim's known Coolify email — several supported providers don't guarantee the registering user actually owns/verified that mailbox (e.g. GitLab with email confirmation disabled, or any IdP the attacker also controls); the attacker completes the OAuth flow, `User::whereEmail(...)` resolves to the victim's existing password-based account, and the attacker is logged in as the victim. **Compounding bug found in the same flow**: `get_socialite_provider()` never checked `OauthSetting::enabled` — that flag was only ever used to decide which login button to show (`FortifyServiceProvider.php`), so a provider an admin explicitly disabled still worked end-to-end via a direct request to its redirect/callback URLs. Confirmed inherited verbatim from the original upstream import for the core email-match logic (`git show` against the base commit) — the `markEmailAsVerified()` call and error-handling improvements added since (2026-07-21) never touched the vulnerable logic. Independently re-verified every claim before fixing: read the actual controller/helper code, confirmed no `provider`/`provider_id` column exists on `users` via the migrations, confirmed `email_verified_at` isn't a reliable signal either (password registration sets it too, via `CreateNewUser`'s non-cloud branch), confirmed the `enabled` flag really is UI-only via `FortifyServiceProvider.php`. Fixed by adding a nullable `oauth_provider` column recording which provider originally created each account (new migration) — an OAuth login now only matches an existing user when it's the *same* provider that created it; a password-only account (`oauth_provider` null) or one created via a different provider is rejected with a clear error instead of silently authenticated. Also added the missing `enabled` check to `get_socialite_provider()`. **Real tradeoff, disclosed rather than hidden**: a user who registered with a password can no longer seamlessly "just use OAuth" for the same email without an explicit account-linking flow (which doesn't exist yet) — refusing silent account linkage is the standard, correct mitigation for this exact vulnerability class, and the convenience cost is far smaller than the account-takeover risk it closes. New `tests/v4/Feature/OauthAccountTakeoverTest.php` (6 tests, zero prior coverage for the login callback flow — the only existing OAuth test covers the settings UI, not login). TDD-proved: reverting the fix reproduces the exact real exploit — the pre-fix code redirects to `/` (successful login) instead of `/login` for the account-takeover test, proving the attacker lands authenticated as the victim, then restored. | 2026-07-26 | Found and fixed live while manually clicking through the app (not via automated testing): all 9 error pages (`400`/`401`/`402`/`403`/`404`/`419`/`429`/`500`/`503`) served genuinely invalid HTML and forced the browser into Quirks Mode. Root cause: every view in `resources/views/errors/` did `@extends('layouts.base')` followed by raw, un-sectioned page content — but `layouts/base.blade.php`'s `<body>` is entirely self-contained inside `@section('body') ... @show` with no `@yield` for a child's content to land in. Blade only renders the *parent* layout after the *child* view's own script finishes, so the un-sectioned content printed to the output buffer immediately — before the parent's own `<!DOCTYPE html>` — putting real page content before the doctype in the final response. Confirmed directly, not just from reading the template: safely reproduced a real 419 (corrupted just the outgoing CSRF token on an isolated Playwright browser context, no shared session/DB state touched) and captured the actual raw response — bare `<div>`, no doctype nearby; live in a real browser, `document.compatMode` read `'BackCompat'` (quirks) and `document.doctype` was `null` before the fix. Every real working standalone page (`auth/login.blade.php` and siblings) instead uses the `<x-layout-simple>` component, which correctly threads content through a `{{ $slot }}` — the 9 error views were the only views in the app not using it. Fixed by converting all 9 to `<x-layout-simple>...</x-layout-simple>`. **Found a secondary issue while fixing**: 8 of the 9 views used `h-full` for vertical centering, which only resolves against an ancestor with a defined height, and nothing in the corrected component chain gives `<body>` one — content rendered top-anchored instead of centered once the doctype bug was fixed. `500.blade.php` (and the real `login.blade.php`) already used `min-h-screen` for the same effect; applied the same fix to the other 8. New test, `tests/v4/Feature/ErrorPageLayoutTest.php` (9 assertions, one per error code): renders each view directly and asserts the output starts with a real `<!doctype html>`; TDD-proved — failed on all 9 against the original code (`'<div class="fle'` instead of `'<!doctype html>'`), passes clean after the fix. Live re-verified afterward too: `document.compatMode` now `'CSS1Compat'`, real doctype present, centering visually restored. Full suite clean: 1,260 Pest (was 1,251 + 9 new), Pint, PHPStan 0 errors. See issue #58 (closed). |

The scan immediately caught three more genuine bugs, none limited to the error pages: (1) `layouts/simple.blade.php`'s `@section('body') ... @parent @endsection` — `@parent` substitutes the parent section's entire raw content at that point, not just its "inner" content, so the parent's own `<body>...</body>` got re-emitted nested inside the child's, producing malformed duplicate `<body>` structure; confirmed via direct `curl` that this hit the real, live login page too, not just error views — fixed by restructuring `layouts/base.blade.php` to a plain `@yield('content')` inside one `<body>`; (2) the theme-init `<script>` sat between `<html>` and `<head>`, invalid placement — moved inside `<head>` as its first child; (3) `<button>` nested inside `<a>` (interactive-in-interactive, invalid HTML5), 17 occurrences across 8 of the 9 error views — converted to a plain `<a class="button">` matching `Button.php`'s own `defaultClass`. | 2026-07-26 | Found live in a real browser session (not a synthetic repro): a genuine 419 on `/logout` after several real login/logout cycles. Root-caused: `AppLayout.jsx`'s sidebar Logout form reads its CSRF `_token` from `document.querySelector('meta[name="csrf-token"]')`, a `<meta>` tag Blade renders exactly once, on the initial full-document load — Inertia's client-side navigation never re-renders `<head>`, and a full-repo grep confirmed nothing anywhere ever updates that tag's value afterward. That token is therefore frozen in the DOM for the entire life of a browser tab, regardless of what happens to the live server session (login/logout elsewhere rotates and regenerates the session's real CSRF token via `session()->regenerate()`/`invalidate()`). A page resurrected from the browser's back/forward cache (bfcache) — a real, common outcome of hitting Back after a login/logout cycle — carries that same frozen, now-stale token, so submitting Logout from it gets rejected by CSRF verification before the app ever sees the request. Attempted to reproduce the exact trigger via Playwright (login → logout → login → browser Back) - headless Chromium re-fetched a fresh dashboard on back-navigation rather than serving a stale bfcache snapshot, so the precise trigger in a real browser (Edge, per the report) couldn't be pinned down further; the underlying staleness itself, however, was independently confirmed directly from the code and is real regardless of which exact DOM-caching mechanism resurrects it. Fixed with the standard mitigation for this whole bug class: a new `reloadOnBFCacheRestore()` (`resources/js/hooks/reloadOnBFCacheRestore.js`), wired into both JS entrypoints (`inertia-app.jsx` and `app.js`), listening for `pageshow` with `event.persisted === true` and forcing `window.location.reload()` - guaranteeing any bfcache-restored page immediately re-fetches a fresh document with a token that matches the live session, before the user could ever act on the stale one. 2 new tests (`reloadOnBFCacheRestore.test.jsx`), TDD-proved (temporarily short-circuited the `persisted` check, confirmed the test failed with the exact symptom, restored). Live-verified in a real Playwright browser session against the actual bundled app: a normal, non-persisted `pageshow` triggers zero reloads (no regression/reload-loop risk), while a genuinely `persisted: true` `pageshow` reliably triggers a real page reload. Full suite clean: 525 Vitest (52 suites, was 523/51), `format:check` clean, `yarn build` clean, ESLint unaffected (confirmed via `git stash` that the pre-existing baseline is actually 23 errors, not the 22 several earlier log entries cite - untouched either way). See issue #60 (closed). |

### Independent verification review (pseudo peer review)

Not real peer review. This is a solo portfolio project — there's no colleague or team available to review the work, and genuine peer review requires another engineer's independent judgment. No automated tool substitutes for that, and this table doesn't claim otherwise.

What's tracked here instead is the closest mechanical substitute actually available: Claude Code's `/code-review` command (a fleet of specialized background subagents, each auditing a diff from a different angle — efficiency, simplification, architectural altitude, reuse, line-by-line diff tracing, repo-convention adherence), run independently against already-merged findings from this session's own code-review cycle, as a second, separate automated pass checking whether the original fix holds up. The cloud-based `/code-review ultra` variant (multi-agent, billed) was attempted first but blocked by a GitHub-App/plan-tier authorization check that couldn't be resolved; the local `/code-review` command (works on any plan, no GitHub App needed) was used instead.

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Why not real peer review | No colleague/team on this solo project. An automated review, however thorough, is not a substitute for another engineer's judgment. |
| What this is instead | `/code-review`, run against an already-merged PR as an independent second look, using a different process than the one that produced the original fix. |
| Coverage so far | 9 code-review/React-test PRs spot-checked (PR #92, PR #94, PR #99, PR #98, PR #100, PR #102, PR #109, PR #111, and the earlier `/code-review 100` pass that accidentally reviewed PR #125's branch instead) |
| Result | **PR #92**: fix confirmed correct and complete across 8 independent review angles — no defect in the fix itself. Surfaced 2 real, minor test-quality issues in an unrelated file from this same session (`DatabaseHealthcheckTab.test.jsx`), both fixed the same day. Also surfaced a non-blocking architectural observation (the hand-maintained sensitive-field redaction list has no structural tie to the model schema) — logged as a candidate for a future backlog card, not yet filed. **PR #94**: found a real, live credential leak the original fix missed — `logdrain_custom_config`/`logdrain_custom_config_parser` weren't redacted, exposing a real embedded Fluent Bit `Authorization Bearer` token to any plain-`read`-scoped API token. Fixed as finding #40 (PR #119) — this one *wasn't* clean, proving the process isn't just rubber-stamping already-done work. **PR #99**: fix confirmed correct across all 5 review angles, but the process found a real, unrelated pre-existing bug in the same function — `skip`/`take` query params crashed the endpoint with a `TypeError` under `strict_types`. Fixed as finding #41 (PR #121). Second real bug found in 3 passes. **`/code-review 100` (first attempt)**: run from the still-open `test/profile-appearance` branch (PR #125), so it reviewed that branch's own diff rather than PR #100's — found a real test-quality gap in `Profile/Appearance.test.jsx`: the active/inactive button-class assertions only ever checked the selected button, never that its sibling lacked the class, so a regression making `optionClass()` ignore its `active` argument would slip through undetected. Fixed the same day, folded directly into PR #125 before merge — third real, non-clean finding this process has surfaced. **PR #98**: the original fix (redacting `ResourcesController`'s previously-unredacted `/resources` endpoint) confirmed correct and complete — no defect in the fix itself, the field lists it added are byte-for-byte correct today. But the review found a real structural drift risk the fix left behind: a fourth, unlinked hand-copy of the same sensitive-field lists already consolidated once via the shared `RedactsApiSensitiveFields` trait for the 3 dedicated controllers — the exact architectural observation first surfaced (but not fixed) during PR #92's review. Fixed as finding #45 (PR #129) — the field lists are now sourced from one place across all 4 controllers, structurally preventing the drift the review warned about. Fourth real, non-clean finding in 5 passes. **PR #100 (run properly this time)**: run from a clean `main` checkout, correcting the earlier attempt's branch mixup. Fix confirmed correct and complete across all 8 review angles — all 4 `ApplicationDeploymentQueue` lookups in `ApplicationDeploymentController.php` correctly scoped to `application_id`, no fifth unscoped lookup missed, no parallel gap in the sibling API `DeployController.php` (already carries its own team_id ownership checks on `deployment_by_uuid()`/`cancel_deployment()`), all 4 new negative tests assert the correct outcome. Independently re-verified before logging clean: confirmed all 4 `->where('application_id', ...)` scopes via direct file read, confirmed `DeployController.php`'s ownership checks are real (`Server::whereTeamId($teamId)`-derived, not just audit-log metadata). Clean — no fix needed, fifth clean-or-real pass out of 6. **PR #102**: this PR's own fix (disabling redirect-following on all 3 outbound webhook jobs) confirmed correct and complete for the specific bypass it targeted. But the review found a real adjacent gap it didn't close: `SendMessageToSlackJob`/`SendMessageToDiscordJob` never re-validate the webhook URL with `SafeWebhookUrl` at send time, unlike `SendWebhookJob` — a DNS-rebinding-style gap independent of the redirect issue this PR fixed. Also flagged (not yet fixed, tracked separately) a real DNS-rebinding limitation in `SafeWebhookUrl` itself, disclosed in PR #102's own commit message as a known gap. Fixed the send-time-validation half as finding #47 (PR #131), extracted the shared validate-and-send trait as finding #48 (PR #132), and closed the disclosed DNS-rebinding gap in `SafeWebhookUrl` itself as finding #49 (PR #133). Fifth real, non-clean finding in 7 passes — three separate fixes from one review pass, the most of any pass this session. **PR #109**: the core fix (removing the `team->id !== 0` IDOR exemption on the `download.backup` route) confirmed correct and complete across all 4 review angles — `currentTeam()` independently re-validates real team membership against the live pivot table, closing off a session-forgery concern one angle raised and another then directly debunked. But the review found a real gap in the fix's own test coverage: the same-team regression test could only assert the route's generic catch-all 500 response, unable to distinguish "authorization passed, SFTP legitimately failed" from "an unrelated bug threw somewhere else in the same block." Fixed as finding #51 (PR #136). Sixth real, non-clean finding in 8 passes. **PR #111**: the core fix (restoring disabled authorization checks across 17 Policy classes) confirmed correct — every other policy's `isAdmin() && teams->contains(...)` pattern verified safe, every controller call site scopes model resolution to `currentTeam()` first. But found two real candidates the original pass left behind: `ServicePolicy::accessTerminal()` missing the null-guard every sibling method in the same file has (fixed as finding #52, PR #137), and a byte-for-byte duplicated pair of private test helpers across two policy test files, fixed as finding #53 (PR #138). Seventh real, non-clean finding in 9 passes. **A follow-up `/code-review 111` re-run** (a second, separate invocation against the same PR) found 3 more instances of the exact same "isAdmin()-only, missing team check" bug shape in 3 different Policy classes — `ApplicationPolicy::update/delete`, `ServicePolicy::delete/forceDelete`, `ApplicationPreviewPolicy::update` — bundled into one fix as finding #54 (PR #139), matching PR #111's own precedent of fixing the same bug across many files in one commit. Eighth real, non-clean finding in this session's pseudo-peer-review process, and the second time a single PR (#111) has produced multiple separate fixes across multiple review passes. **PR #135**: the core fix (adding the missing `authorize('view', $githubApp)` call, closing the critical read-only secret-disclosure hole) confirmed correct and complete. But the review found the fix's own new team-membership check on `update()`/`delete()` used the wrong helper (`isAdmin()`, session-team-scoped, instead of `isAdminOfTeam($teamId)`, target-team-scoped) — a narrower cross-tenant gap than the one PR #135 closed, but real and independently confirmed exploitable via a live HTTP request. Fixed as finding #56 (PR #147). Ninth real, non-clean finding in 11 passes. |

The one real, minor candidate: `Project/{Application,Database,Service}/Configuration.jsx` each statically import every tab component (12/fewer/fewer) instead of `React.lazy()`-loading only the active one — biggest chunk affected is Application's at 69.20 kB. Not Tier 1 or Tier 2 by this session's own tiering (no security/reliability impact, modest absolute savings) — deliberately deprioritized below the security/reliability-first review order. Not yet started — Backlog (#116) |
| 16 | No React Error Boundaries anywhere in the app | Found 2026-08-03 via direct user observation, not a bug — confirmed zero components implement `componentDidCatch`/`getDerivedStateFromError` anywhere in `resources/js/`. With Inertia, React stays mounted across page navigations, so any single component throwing during render currently blanks the *entire* page with no recovery until a manual reload — no natural full-reload safety net between pages the way a traditional multi-page app gets for free. Design note for whenever this is picked up: a single root-level boundary is better than nothing but still takes down the whole shell (including nav chrome) on any one widget's error — the more valuable version wraps several regions independently (page content separate from `AppLayout.jsx`'s persistent nav/sidebar chrome). Not yet started — Backlog (#126) |
| 17 | DNS-rebinding TOCTOU gap in `SafeWebhookUrl` (disclosed, not fixed) | Found 2026-08-03 during finding #49's fix (PR #133) — resolving a webhook URL's hostname at validation time closes the common SSRF case, but the actual outbound request moments later does its own independent DNS lookup, so an attacker controlling authoritative DNS with a near-zero TTL could theoretically rebind between the two. Disclosed directly in `SafeWebhookUrl`'s own docblock. Closing it for real needs connection-level IP pinning (`CURLOPT_RESOLVE`/Guzzle's `curl` `resolve` option, with TLS SNI/cert-validation implications to work through) — a materially bigger change than the DNS-resolution fix itself. Low priority: requires active timing precision around the validate/send window, not just DNS control. Not yet started — Backlog (#134) |

### Fresh-clone end-to-end boot test (deferred 2026-07-13 — destructive, run when losing dev data is acceptable)

The first-boot automation (`php artisan dev --init`) is covered by feature tests and an idempotent live run, but has **not** been proven with a true from-scratch boot the way a real cloner would experience it — doing so wipes every named volume (all dev projects/servers/applications, the dev database, backups, MinIO data). Steps, when ready:

```bash
# 0. Commit/push everything first. This destroys all local dev data.
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.dev.yml down -v

# 1. Simulate a fresh cloner's .env (APP_KEY intentionally empty in the template)
cp .env.development.example .env

# 2. First boot — init runs composer install, migrate, dev --init automatically
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d

# 3. Wait for the app to report healthy, then verify
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.dev.yml ps
curl -s http://localhost:8000/api/health
```

Expected: `APP_KEY` now populated in `.env` (written by `key:generate` through the bind mount), login works at `http://localhost:8000` with `test@example.com` / `password`, and no `coolify-proxy` container yet (the app creates it at runtime — see `DEVELOPING_IN_CONTAINERS_WINDOWS.md` §2). Caveats: cached `coolify:dev`/`coolify-realtime:dev`/`coolify-testing-host:dev` images make this test skip the image-build path — to also prove a from-scratch **build**, remove those images first and expect the possible `NGINX_VERSION` pin issue documented in `docs/command.md`'s WSL2-migration section, step 6.

### Verification standing habit

- Every change in this repo is expected to go through: `vendor/bin/pint --dirty --format agent`, `vendor/bin/phpstan analyse`, `php artisan test --compact`, and `yarn build` before being considered done. See `docs/command.md` for the exact commands.
